589d79e40a45.title: Judge Lets Hacker Behind Massive GTA 6 Leak of 2022 Go Free With a Warning: 'Don't Let This Happen Again'
589d79e40a45.summary: The hacker behind the massive GTA 6 leak in September 2022 has been released on license with a strong warning from the judge.
589d79e40a45.content: The hacker behind the massive GTA 6 leak in September 2022 has been released on license with a strong warning from the judge. Having already served the majority of his seven year sentence, Arion Kurtaj, from Oxford in the United Kingdom, was allowed to go free, conditionally. According to the BBC , the judge warned Kurtaj: "Don't let this happen again." Kurtaj attempted to extort GTA 6 developer Rockstar Games in 2022. After socially engineering his way into the company Slack, the now 21-year-old threatened to release clips of the unfinished game unless Rockstar paid a ransom. He pleaded guilty to the hacking offenses , which he carried out when he was 16 and 17 years old, earlier this week. ⚖️ Arion Kurtaj, 21, has been convicted today for targeting major international companies, hacking into their private systems, stealing information and data, and causing millions of dollars in losses. 📰 https://t.co/UvJTCFWnct https://t.co/3CoLIw7dDs — Crown Prosecution Service (@CPSUK) November 16, 2026 Originally, Kurtaj was sentenced to an indefinite stay in a prison hospital due to his autism diagnosis. After reconsideration, he was deemed fit to stand trial and spent the remainder of his time in a traditional prison, starting in January. With his release, Kurtaj has been given a Serious Crime Prevention Order, which restricts his interactions online, barring him from using social apps like Telegram and Discord, in an attempt to prevent him working with hacker groups. The order will last for five years. The hack happened while Kurtaj was already under police protection in a Travelodge with his computer confiscated. During his stay, he used an Amazon Fire Stick and the hotel television to hack Rockstar, Revolut, and Uber. The GTA 6 hack saw him steal 90 clips of an unfinished build well before Rockstar was ready to show gameplay from its anticipated open-world sequel, which launched last week. It resulted in the first major GTA 6 leak, as early gameplay footage was shared online. Here, we saw dual protagonists Jason and Lucia for the first time. These clips were shared under the online name TeaPotUberHacker. It would be over a year before Rockstar finally showed the protagonists itself, and even longer until we got an official gameplay reveal, which was only shared in August of this year. "If Rockstar does not contact me on Telegram within 24 hours I will start releasing the source code," he said in the company Slack. When the company didn’t respond, he released the files, costing the company $5 million in damages. Just getting started in GTA 6 or wondering what to do next? d19339025ff8.title: GTA 6’s Best-Kept Secret Is the Key to Its Whole Design
d19339025ff8.summary: Rockstar kept a reveal in GTA 6's prologue a secret for years, but now we all know it, it's clear how it guides the game's entire design.
d19339025ff8.content: Warning: this story contains spoilers for GTA 6’s prologue and Chapter 1. In the final months of trailers, screenshots, and extended looks leading up to Grand Theft Auto 6 ’s launch, Rockstar was keeping a huge secret. It had revealed Jason and Lucia to the world years before and, by the summer of this year, we knew that their romantic relationship was core to the story. But until the moment the game went live, we had no idea that the pair were parents. As we all found out in the prologue, Jason and Lucia have a son, Tomás. And more than just a baby, this little infant is the key to GTA 6’s entire design ethos. Historically, Rockstar has drawn from classic crime movie tropes to establish the themes of its stories. Tommy Vercetti cut through all in his path on his way to becoming Miami’s premier crime lord. Carl Johnson rallied the boys in the hood on his quest for revenge. And Niko Bellic put his war-honed killing skills to work on the streets of Liberty City. While there are elements of relatability in all these stories – hurt over dead mothers, discovering the lie of the American dream – you’d be in the tiny minority of players if you could claim to truly recognise the lives of GTA’s protagonists as reflections of your own timeline. But things are different this time. As Lucia orders another free water at her local cafe, her RydeMe app notifies her that her driver account has been suspended. With the cost of living rising and the job market increasingly unstable in the real world, Lucia’s reality is just a step away from ours. As a then-single mother with a baby’s life on the line, the thing that pushes her towards serious crime isn’t the lust for power or infinite riches – it’s the simple need for survival. It’s the most relatable and realistic starting point any GTA has delivered. Later in Chapter 1, after being introduced to Mattia and Kat and their extravagant lifestyle, we do see Lucia pine for money in a more classic GTA manner. The lure of the never-ending party is difficult to ignore after nine months behind bars. But the act that put Lucia in jail is key: before holding up the store, she ejects every bullet from her magazine and clears the pistol’s chamber. She has no intention of murder. All she wants is to afford rent and feed her baby. Similarly, Jason is far from the hardened gangster that we’ve historically seen in GTA. While he’s more involved in the criminal scene than Lucia, for him it’s just a job. Staying away from regular employment because of his awkward military history, he finds cash-in-hand wages via Brian’s drug-running operations. While there are sparks every now and again, it’s a low-level job – practically an Amazon driver for a middleman. This helps ground Jason in a more familiar reality; he’s just looking for a simple life, emphasised by GTA 6’s encouraged morning routine of shower, coffee, and a workout. As the innocent emotional stake of the entire piece, Tomás encourages a more realistic depiction of our two protagonists. Tomás is emblematic of all this. As the innocent emotional stake of the entire piece, he encourages a more realistic depiction of our two protagonists. And that increased realism flows into the gameplay systems, mission design, and open-world opportunities. While it would be foolish to suggest that Tomás was the idea that began GTA 6’s pursuit of incredibly detailed realism, he is the character that makes the design feel complete and authentic, despite barely being a part of the story. bb20beff33b9.title: GTA 6 Leaker Cyberleek Reportedly Releases .exe File for Xbox Build, Sparking Concern an Unofficial PC Port Could Be Around the Corner
bb20beff33b9.summary: Cyberleek has reportedly made good on their promise and released the executable file for the leaked Xbox build of GTA 6, sparking concern that an unofficial PC port could be around the corner.
bb20beff33b9.content: Cyberleek has reportedly made good on their promise and released the executable file for the leaked Xbox build of GTA 6 , sparking concern that an unofficial PC port could be around the corner. The infamous hacker had vowed to release the .exe for the incomplete GTA 6 Xbox build whether the Cyberleek memecoin hit its market cap target or not , and now it is out in the wild, some within the homebrew scene are preparing to take a close look at it. Cyberleek released the exe with a fresh statement insisting their actions on GTA 6 so far were about “fighting anti-consumerism in the games industry.” Cyberleek also taunts Rockstar parent company Take-Two’s so-far unsuccessful effort to prevent further leaks or, it seems, track down those responsible, saying: “Months of takedowns, subpoenas and wallet tracing later, the hunt is still on and the uploads keep arriving.” They also pushed back on claims the GTA 6 leaks are about little more than pushing a crypto scheme, insisting that crypto was used to generate funds for a secret project outside of the game. “There is no other way to move funds without names,” Cyberleek said, “and this work requires no names.” Some are now predicting that AI-assisted recompilation of the leaked Xbox build could result in GTA 6 on PC in just days, with performance improvements over the console version in weeks. This is of course a nightmare scenario for Take-Two and Sony and Microsoft, which are benefiting greatly from GTA 6 releasing on console only. The console version of GTA 6 targets 30fps across all platforms, although struggles at times to hit that on base PS5, and Xbox Series X and S. As a result, there is huge interest in a potential PC version offering 60fps gameplay. The release of the Xbox build from this month runs counter to the thought that Cyberleek only had access to an early development build of GTA 6, a feeling that was reinforced not only by the videos that were released in the summer, but by the differences that have emerged following the game’s official launch. Fans are calling on people not to spend money on Cyberleek, pointing out the leaker cashed out back in August and did again in October. Analysis of cryptocurrency transactions in late August pointed to the GTA 6 leaker cashing out having earnt around $270,000. IGN had reported on fan skepticism around the alleged leaked gameplay that reportedly showed both Jason and Lucia fully naked . A previous leaked gameplay video allegedly showed a tank spawning into the world, which suggested access to a dev menu of some kind. The leaked videos allegedly showing both Jason and Lucia fully naked also show NPCs failing to react to that in any way, which suggested this effect was achieved with either a dev menu or cheats. In the wake of Cyberleek’s initial leaks, Take-Two issued subpoenas to the likes of Discord as part of its search for the person or group of people responsible. It remains unclear how the gameplay footage, any potential build of the game it was taken from, or this latest Xbox build, escaped the confines of Rockstar's infamous tight security. In August, Rockstar addressed the GTA 6 leaks , describing the situation as "heartbreaking" for its development team and "unfortunate" for fans. At the time, the developer acknowledged that its intended experience for players "may now be impacted by some spoilers," but reiterated GTA 6's previously-confirmed launch date of November 19.

525ba0d2fc75.title: Family-Friendly Fortnite Streamer Goes Viral After Picking Up GTA 6 And Performing the Ultimate Heelturn, Including a Bloody Zoo Rampage
525ba0d2fc75.summary: Nice-guy Fortnite streamer Nick Eh 30 has gone viral after trying GTA 6 — and immediately pushing the violence in Rockstar's game to its limit.
525ba0d2fc75.content: Nice-guy Fortnite streamer Nick Eh 30 has gone viral after trying GTA 6 — and immediately pushing the violence in Rockstar's game to its limit. For almost a decade, cheery Canadian streamer Nicholas " Nick Eh 30 " Amyoony has amassed a community of millions around his family-friendly Fortnite streams. His personal brand is based on pushing positivity, he's known for never swearing on camera, and he's become one of the few Twitch stars partnered with Epic Games to get a skin of himself made available in-game. So it has, understandably, come as something of a surprise to see wholesome Nick Eh 30 embracing the most dastardly deeds GTA 6 has on offer: kicking pet dogs to death in the street , shooting animals in the zoo , and walking down the length of a train executing every passenger at point blank range . As someone who has followed Nick Eh 30 for a while, seeing him wandering around GTA 6's world eliminating swathes of its animal population while chuckling to himself is indeed odd to see. Social media is awash with similar reactions, with posts from his followers stating things like: "IN WHAT UNIVERSE DO YOU NEED TO BE DOING THIS" and "Years of building ramps in Fortnite could not prepare chat for this." But this is all clearly intentional, down to his streams being labelled as humorously promising "family friendly GTA" gameplay (I'm not sure there's any such thing). And the fact this has led people to actually discuss his streams and share clips further has only proven why he's likely doing this. NickEh30 takes a taser to the Zoo in GTA VI https://t.co/4SAVgUCjYm — yoxic (@yoxics) November 22, 2026 All of that said, it's still a surprise to see Nick squarely aiming for the game's brutal "Irredeemable" criminal profile rating — a label that Rockstar has actually made quite difficult to achieve unless you really, really want to play the game as bloodily as possible. It's this, seemingly, which has led to clips of Nick playing fetch with dogs using lumps of C4 , and throwing random NPCs from buildings . Just getting started in GTA 6 or wondering what to do next? e62602da3146.title: The Definitive Proof That GTA 6 and Red Dead Redemption Share The Same Universe
e62602da3146.summary: Here are the seven easter eggs in GTA 6 that prove Red Dead Redemption and Grand Theft Auto take place in the same universe.
e62602da3146.content: From action movies to popular memes, there are dozens and dozens of Easter eggs and references to wider pop culture in GTA 6. But Rockstar has also slipped in more than a few nods to some of the studio’s previous games within Leonida. There’s a Manhunt-themed tattoo, for example, and a ludicrously convoluted secret that has already been unearthed involving a portal back to the days of Vice City. But one series is showing up more than others: Red Dead Redemption. We’re still working our way through finding all of them, as is the rest of the internet, but so far we’ve found seven secrets that relate to the developer’s beloved Western games. From hats and guns to road names and license plates, here are seven Red Dead Easter eggs in GTA 6. Valentine Drive If you’re looking for hidden details about Red Dead, the Western-themed Frontier Mini Golf course is a natural place to start. While none of the holes directly tell the tale of Red Dead Revolver, Red Dead Redemption, or its prequel—aside from squinting at hole four and seeing a snowy train wreck as a tangential nod to RDR2’s prologue—there are still things to find. We’ll get on to who can be seen roaming it in a moment, but before you even set foot inside, an Easter egg can be found. That’s because the attraction itself is located on Valentine Drive, a reference to the first major town you explore in Chapter 1 of Red Dead Redemption 2’s story. This is the location where Arthur famously drinks a few too many beers, has a bit of a dance, and looks for his friend, Lenny. Sadly, alcohol doesn’t seem to be served at this Mini Golf, although there’s nothing stopping you from bringing your own six-pack in. Tiny Arthur Morgan Once you’re on the course, though, a little friend with a familiar face riding on his back may well walk up to you. A small chihuahua with a cowboy toy, dressed in remarkably similar clothing to what Red Dead Redemption 2 protagonist Arthur Morgan wore in many of the game’s trailers. Feel free to give the little guy a pet, too, and his gun-toting rider will look like he’s giving it a little “yeehaw”. Adorable. Arthur’s Hat Perhaps more life-sized Arthur Morgan Easter eggs are more your thing, though. Well, get yourself over to Port Gellhorn to get your hands on, and head in, one such thing. Follow the trail of signs and balloons to find a resident looking to get rid of any old tat. Hidden amongst it all, though, is a real treasure. No, not the cow-patterned Hawaiian shirt, but something that will make fans of Red Dead Redemption 2’s hearts flutter a little: a genuine cowboy hat. Not just any cowboy, either, but Arthur himself. The dark brown colour, complete with twisted rope around the rim, is unmistakable, and is now Jason or Lucia’s to wear whenever they like. An absolute bargain at $35, too. Duke Arms As if we needed any further proof that the Grand Theft Auto and Red Dead Redemption stories take place in the same universe, the Duke Arms Company cements this. At any of Leonida’s Ammu-Nation stores, you can find weapons made by the same gun company that produced the Duke 1853 Navy Revolver in Red Dead Online. On the packaging found inside GTA 6’s gun stores, you can also spot 1853 written out in Roman numerals (MDCCCLIII) on the boxes. It just can’t be a coincidence. Flaco Hern á ndez and Blackwater “The Cowboy’s Prayer is To Die Young” is a Wild West-set novel of which you can read a few pages in GTA 6. There are a few fun little details hidden within. First, a mention of Blackwater, the port city from Red Dead Redemption and its prequel, where John Marston chooses to build his ranch near to. But there’s also a familiar name to those who chose to fully engage with RDR2’s side activities. Flaco Hernández was an infamous outlaw who you can meet during the 2018 game’s “The Noblest of Men, and a Woman” stranger mission. 9259c0358563.title: Should You Trust Halifax in GTA 6?
9259c0358563.summary: Should you trust Halifax in GTA 6's chapter three mission, Dubious Provenance? We have the answer.
9259c0358563.content: Warning: Spoilers for the Dubious Provenance mission in chapter three of GTA 6 follow. GTA 6 is full of choices, big and small. In fact, the whole way you choose to play the game is a choice, whether that be as an ultraviolet psychopath or a more professional class of criminal. Or if you decide that Jason and Lucia are a couple hopelessly head-over-heels in love, or more platonic partners in crime. Some choices, however, are much more binary, with instant effects tied to them. One of the clearest examples of this is presented to you during a chapter three mission called Dubious Provenance. Should you trust Halifax or not? The answer is twofold: the smart decision is to reject his offer, but the much more fun option is to place your faith in him. Let me explain. Dubious Provenance kicks off by driving all the way to the fancy town of Capri, found in the east of Leonida, and home to the sort of houses Jason and Lucia can only dream of living in at this point in their story. Just by the centre of town is an antiques store where you’re tasked with bringing the mysterious statue that has fallen into your possession to be valued. Halifax, a man with a fairly convincing British accent, overhears your conversation with the shop’s owner, Evelyn, and offers you a deal. While she isn’t interested in the statue, he most definitely is, telling you that he will get it valued for you if you hand it over. Now, despite his smart appearance, all is not what it seems with Halifax, and without spoiling it too much, he’s not exactly the antiques expert he claims to be. The smart, and arguably correct, choice from a story perspective is to reject him. But the much more fun and beneficial option (if you’re a collectibles hunter) is to accept. Accepting adds a couple more main missions to the Dubious Provenance story rather than just ending it there and then. You’ll also receive the Crowex Octane “Bobby Ambrose” unique watch in return. This is a missable collectible otherwise. But more importantly, you get two more very fun missions to play through. The first includes a stealthy infiltration and a massive, and I mean, massive revelation about Halifax. The second is one of the best chase sequences in GTA 6, scored hilariously to a great bit of contrapuntal music. For full spoilers and a step-by-step guide, you can check out our walkthrough . If you reject, you won’t get the watch, but you will have a second shot at playing through these missions. Halifax will later contact you and give you the option to phone him if you change your mind, transforming these main missions into optional ones. These must be completed by the end of chapter three , or they’ll disappear forever, though. Ultimately, the choice to accept or reject comes down to whether you want the watch or not. Of course, you can choose to just never contact him again if you’re desperate to progress through the story as quickly as possible, but you will miss out on a great bit of fun as a result. So, should you trust Halifax during Dubious Provenance? I’d say yes; it’s a much more fun road to take if you’re looking to squeeze every bit of enjoyment out of GTA 6. d8fe3705a9c1.content: Strip Clubs are part of the very DNA of GTA 6 , and exotic dance chain Spearmint Rhino is making the most of it, hiring a choreographer to recreate the moves of the in-game dancers for its patrons. According to the club, it's in response to a wave of requests from visitors and people sliding into its DMs. "I’m fascinated with the attention to detail from Rockstar," said the head choreographer, Brooke Wilde. "I spent hours in Jack of Hearts and Delights Cabaret, mastering each performance to bring back to Spearmint, and now obsessed gamers can put down their controllers, get out of the bedroom, and experience their favourite virtual lap dances with the Spearmint Rhino girls in the real world. While the in-game strip clubs are addictive, nothing beats the real thing.” While we can't be sure exactly how many people are reaching out to their local strip joints for IRL GTA-inspired bodily contact, you have to respect the hustle. It's also an interesting counterpoint given GTA 6's impact on another part of the adult entertainment industry, with Mashable reporting that Pornhub saw a 15.5% drop an hour after the game was released on November 19. Spearmint Rhino's relationship with the series actually goes back to 2013 and GTA 5, when Rockstar used a play on the name of the clubs, Vanilla Rhino, and Rockstar has said that developers for GTA 6 visited strip clubs in Miami and Florida (where Spearmint Rhino has one of its venues) for research purposes. In GTA 6, Jason and Lucia can both go to strip clubs either together as a couple or individually, and can opt-in for VIP lap dances. As explained in our GTA 6 sex and romance guide , you can throw money at dancers, and if you throw most of your money at one dancer they will remove some of their clothes. “While gamers across the world immerse themselves in virtual worlds, demand for authentic real-world experiences has never been higher and we’ve had hundreds of inquiries from GTA 6 fans," explained the company president and COO, Kathy Vercher. "Strip clubs are such an iconic feature in the franchise, and Spearmint Rhino is uniquely positioned to create a real-world experience for gamers. Thanks to the dedication of our Chief Choreographer, Brooke, we’ve been able to bring the in-game lap dance experience into our venues worldwide, with such accuracy that gamers are guaranteed to get a mindblowing real-life experience.” Just getting started in GTA 6 or wondering what to do next? c77d02ebbf8b.title: Over Half of GTA 6 Watch Time Came From Viewers Under 25 Years Old
c77d02ebbf8b.summary: The bulk of fans watching streams of GTA 6 are under 25 years old, according to recent stats compiled by StreamsCharts.
c77d02ebbf8b.content: The bulk of fans watching streams of GTA 6 are under 25 years old, according to recent stats compiled by StreamsCharts. After 13 long years, GTA 6 is finally out in the wild. Rockstar’s highly-anticipated release has already broken numerous records, one of the most impressive being that it became the single most popular game ever on both Twitch and Kick just 26 hours after its global release. Now that it’s had a little time to breathe, more data is rolling in, including information about who’s watching streamers play the game. StreamsCharts , a data analytics company that studies games-focused streaming platforms, discovered that most viewers of GTA 6 broadcasts tend to trend under the age of 25. According to Streamlabs’ stats, 30.8% of viewers in GTA 6 streams are 20 - 24 years old, making up the bulk of those watching the game across Kick, Twitch, and YouTube. (Painfully, StreamsCharts pointed out that these players were in elementary school when GTA 5 came out.) 16.8% of these viewers are 17 - 19, with 8.5% accounting for viewers 16 or under. The second-largest age range watching GTA 6 streams are viewers aged 25 - 29. 11.6% of viewers are 30 - 34, and the numbers keep dropping from there. StreamsCharts also found that an overwhelming majority of these viewers are single men, accounting for 83.8% of the gender divide. That’s not to say that gals aren’t also watching streamers play Rockstar’s latest; 14% of viewers are female, and if you’ve been on social media lately, you’ve probably seen a fair few female players showing off their outfits for Jason and Lucia or the viral conversation about how it’s, oddly, comparable to a crime-focused version of The Sims. Perhaps unsurprisingly, the United States makes up the bulk of GTA 6 viewership. Brazil isn’t far behind, coming in at 12.4% of the game’s total audience; Spain and Germany follow at 6.9% and 6.8%, respectively. Certain games have also experienced a drop in viewership following GTA 6’s release. StreamsCharts found that GTA 5 had the sharpest drop-off on Twitch, followed by the platform’s Just Chatting category and World of Warcraft. The GTA hype train is in full swing, and it’s making big bucks for Rockstar. The company reportedly made a staggering $3.79 billion from the game in just 24 hours, making it the single biggest entertainment launch in history. Internet provider Comcast even revealed that it experienced its highest-traffic day ever as players downloaded the game to their consoles, and PlayStation confirmed that GTA 6 was its biggest game launch in the company’s history. cdf8ec2943d6.title: Cyberpunk 2 Is Still a Ways Out, but CD Projekt Red Says Its RPGs Will Come Out Faster in the Future
cdf8ec2943d6.summary: We are still two years out from The Witcher 4, but Ciri's big breakout adventure isn't the only massive RPG cooking at CD Projekt Red. It sounds like development on Cyberpunk 2 is carrying on smoothly, though it's still very early in its development cycle.
cdf8ec2943d6.content: We are still two years out from The Witcher 4 , but Ciri's big breakout adventure isn't the only massive RPG cooking at CD Projekt Red. It sounds like development on Cyberpunk 2 is carrying on smoothly, though it's still very early in its development cycle. In a November 24 earnings call , CD Projekt Red VP of Strategy & Investor Relations Karolina Gnaś said the team is "making good progress with Cyberpunk 2, we are happy with where we are, but it's still too early to give a specific date and plan on when we will move onto full production." Although she couldn't provide a clear date when we'll hear more about the game, she did add that the studio plans to have around 200 developers by the end of 2026 and 320 by the end of next year. It is admittedly a bit early to expect any kind of information about the Cyberpunk sequel, but it has been simmering in the background since at least 2022 , and it sounds like CD Projekt Red wants to speed up development of its massive RPGs. In its consolidated earnings report , CD Projekt Red admitted that most of its games "normally take 3 to 6 years to produce," mostly due to working on one game at a time. But that strategy has since changed. In that same report, the company said, "At the moment, the CD Projekt Red studio is working in parallel on several productions (also in collaboration with external development teams) and supporting products, which is expected to translate into shorter intervals between the releases of subsequent titles in the future." Whether or not that new timeline will affect Cyberpunk 2 is the question. But even if that faster development timeline is in effect for Cyberpunk 2, it's likely we'll still have to wait a while to actually see it in the wild. In an earnings report last year, when Cyberpunk 2 entered pre-production, CD Projekt CEO Michał Nowakowski suggested that CDPR's games take four or five years to move from pre-production to release, which would put the game somewhere in 2030 or 2031. And given that the game still hasn't entered full production, it isn't likely we're going to see some sort of rapid release after the Witcher 4 in 2028. We're probably going to be waiting a little while longer for Cyberpunk 2, but it's already sounding like the game is taking shape. Just last month, associate game director Pawel Sasko revealed that a lot of the developers working on Cyberpunk 2 are former modders. Sasko went on to claim that "the modding community is really keeping [Cyberpunk 2077] alive," so hopefully that energy translates to Cyberpunk 2 – whenever it comes out.

f43e47a2c2d6.title: 'Crazy Secretive' — GTA 6 Voice Actor Reveals Details of Rockstar's 'Humongous' NDA
f43e47a2c2d6.summary: A voice actor who appeared in GTA 6 described the wild non-disclosure agreement she had to sign before working on the game, calling the project “crazy secretive.”
f43e47a2c2d6.content: A voice actor who appeared in GTA 6 described the wild non-disclosure agreement she had to sign before working on the game, calling the project “crazy secretive.” Issa Lopez is a voice actor who plays a radio host on GTA 6’s fictional Cocoteo FM radio station, a Latin channel that plays reggaeton and dembow tracks featuring Spanish-speaking artists from the Caribbean and Latin America. In a November 20 interview with Page Six , Lopez revealed that she recorded her lines for the station as recently as September 2026, and said the NDA she was made to sign before officially performing the part was comparable to the process of purchasing a home or a vehicle. “Have you ever signed papers to buy a house? To buy a car? You know, it’s thick! It was a pretty humongous pack of papers that came with it. But I mean, it’s worth it! And I didn’t have to wait like all these other folks. Some of these folks have been working on this for like 10–11 years, you know what I mean?” she said. She went on to describe the recording process for her lines, saying that she hadn’t seen anything until the day of the performance. With no time to prepare, she was essentially “put on the spot” — but she was so excited about the opportunity that she didn’t mind. “In my usual voiceover gigs — let’s say you want me to do a commercial for you. I get a Zoom [link] maybe the day before, maybe the same day I get the script,” she explained. “Everything was like, popped up on the screen. It was mad cool. It was like, ‘You ready? And I’m like, ‘Uh-huh.’ You press a button and then boop, it pops on the screen, they say hello, and there’s a bunch of people in your ear. And they’re like, ‘Okay, here it is,’ and that’s when you see it. You are put on the spot. And you better bring it. And after that, I don’t know — whatever was in front of my face disappeared. “ Lopez revealed that she wasn’t told what the project was for, but figured it out based on context clues from an email titled “heard by millions,” saying she “read it and knew what it was for.” She also didn’t know that Bad Bunny would be co-hosting the Cocoteo station alongside her, leading to a wild realization once Rockstar released the radio stations before the game actually came out. “We knew nothing. I saw the liners, and when I saw the liners I was like, ‘Okay, I know why I got the gig.’ ‘Cause it was like Puerto Rican dot com. It was super easy. But it was so cool, because Rockstar let me be myself. …they were like, ‘Issa, we want natural. Whatever you got, we want,'" she said. The actors in GTA 6 were extremely secretive about their involvement in the project. Most notably, actress Manni L. Perez, who plays Lucia, was under immense pressure after fans sleuthed her social media accounts and figured out it was her before she could officially reveal the information. Now, she’s up for best performance at The Game Awards, which is one of eight nominations the game has secured mere weeks before the show takes place this December. Other performers who have finally revealed their involvement in the game are Mandy’s actress, Lexie Shoaibi , as well as the voice and performance artist for Jason Duval, Dylan Rourke . Rockstar released the full credits for the game, too, which you can check out here — just beware of spoilers if you haven’t finished it yet. a1633ea34175.title: Some GTA 6 Fans Love Chapter 1 for Its Slower Pace and Are Spending Dozens of Hours Roleplaying in It
a1633ea34175.summary: GTA 6's first chapter has been somewhat divisive due to its slower pace, but it's also a part of the game that some fans have spent dozens of hours playing due to it highly immersive slice-of-life elements.
a1633ea34175.content: Warning: This article features light spoilers for the early hours of GTA 6 . GTA 6's first chapter has been somewhat divisive due to its slower pace, but it's also a part of the game that some fans have spent dozens of hours playing due to it highly immersive slice-of-life elements. Instead of throwing you headfirst into crazy heists or explosive set pieces, the first chapter of GTA 6 is largely spent bumbling around Rockstar's version of the Florida Keys. You can go fishing, scuba diving, and even fix up your house before Lucia's release from prison. It's an exceptionally low-key and chill opening to a game filled with all kinds of crazy action, which is why it's also rubbed some people the wrong way. They don't want to do chores or kick it on the beach; they want to cause some mayhem. However, for others, this has become an unexpected hook for GTA 6 that actually delayed their interest in getting to the meat of Rockstar's open-world epic. Various fans of the game have said they spent anywhere from 10 to as many as 40+ hours in just Chapter 1 alone. Keep in mind, this is a sliver of the overall experience, and much of the game's most interesting activities don't get added until subsequent chapters. However, some players just enjoyed living inside of this part of the game before things go horribly wrong and they're forced to start ramping up the violence and crime. "Best thing about that early chapter is just how low stakes and casual it feels," said X user @CS11__ after spending 41 hours in Chapter 1 alone. "I forced myself not to go farther than Hamlet, so I really only ever experienced these two small areas in 40 hours. [...] The game hardly opened up, but it still felt unbelievably rich and fun." But... what is it these people are actually doing, if not blowing stuff up and creating tons of chaos? Some fans were just going through the motions, giving themselves daily routines that involved working out, taking on relaxing hobbies, and exploring. "[A] lot of roleplaying, day-to-day living type stuff," said Aaron Espionza on X , who estimated that he spent around 15–18 hours before picking up Lucia from prison. "I had a routine even when I would wake up, drive to the juice bar down the street, get my orange juice, and then say hello to the locals. If anyone said anything mean, I would get violent and throw empty juice cups at them. [I] did the workout routines. Basketball was a favorite of mine. Side stuff with Cal fishing, Donnie pick-ups, and scuba. But so much of it was testing how much detail Rockstar put into it. 'If I do this , will they do that ?' type of systems exploration. Always came away surprised." X user @scaasm noted that the lower stakes nature of Chapter 1 even prompted him to follow traffic laws and use manual turn signals in GTA 6: "I follow traffic laws unless I'm doing something criminal, and generally just taking it very slow. [I'm] loving every moment." The location itself was also a big driving point for a lot of fans, some of whom have personal connections or apprecation for its real life counterpart: "As someone from Florida, I think the Keys is one of those locations that they absolutely nailed (waning sands outlets too; they look exactly like the Orlando ones)," said @piterparker69 on X . "It felt kinda uncanny driving around (especially the 7 Mile Bridge) because of how good it replicates real life." "I have been obsessed with the Florida Keys for the last 5 years, and finding out you spend the start of the game there, catching fish, fixing my house, working out, and just vibing gave me little motivation to move on," said @AnchormanV2 on X after spending roughly a dozen hours in Chapter 1. "I took my sweet time in Key Lento, not necessarily to avoid progressing the story, but more so [bcause] I was just having so much fun exploring the keys and just taking it all in," said X user @HorrorUntitled . 2feda3b8ec94.title: Max Verstappen Spent 40 Hours Playing GTA 6 and Still Won the Las Vegas Grand Prix
2feda3b8ec94.summary: Famous Dutch-Belgian race driver Max Verstappen revealed that he’d spent the weekend of the Las Vegas Grand Prix locked in to GTA 6, saying he played over 40 hours of the game.
2feda3b8ec94.content: Famous Dutch-Belgian race driver Max Verstappen revealed that he’d spent the weekend of the Las Vegas Grand Prix locked in to GTA 6, saying he played over 40 hours of the game. Everyone’s got GTA 6 fever, including Max Verstappen. Not even the Las Vegas Grand Prix could stop him from causing virtual chaos in Vice City, which he says he spent more than 40 hours doing during the weekend of the race. Verstappen nonchalantly dropped this nugget of information during a live stream the following week, saying he would play the game in the mornings and evenings in between his duties on the track. “I played a lot in the evening and in the morning in Vegas,” Verstappen explained. “I mean, I can’t go out anyways and walk around.” The driver also revealed that he’s been so focused on GTA 6 and driving real-life race cars that he’s “completely forgotten” how to play Minecraft, despite having a scheduled stream for it. “I’m so bad when I play too many games at the same time. I can’t, I just can’t!” he joked. 🤯Max Verstappen played GTA VI for FORTY HOURS while in Las Vegas On top of that, he also won the race https://t.co/jwuxQnHxyS — Pablo Martinez (Holiness) (@F1BigData) November 24, 2026 The Las Vegas Grand Prix took place on November 19 - 21. Verstappen took first place in the prestigious Formula 1 race, beating out Britain’s Lando Norris and Australia’s Oscar Piastri. The race is around 50 laps long with a total race distance of 192.6 miles (309.96 kilometers), generally lasting around one and a half hours. As revealed by the name, Grand Theft Auto is a game series that involves a lot of vehicles, and not just for carjacking; the latest entry in the franchise even features drag racing and mudding, a hobby common in the American countryside that involves the use of off-road vehicles racing through mud-covered areas or even specially-made racetracks. It’s quite likely that Verstappen dabbled a bit in these side missions, though he says that he’s already beaten 80% of GTA 6’s story. In fact, the driver admitted that he has skipped most of the main cutscenes, calling them “too boring.” Verstappen’s style of playing GTA 6 is one of several that we’ve seen over the weekend. In fact, many players are avoiding progressing the story in favor of spending time in Chapter 1, which sees Jason living the average life of a drug runner in Rockstar’s fictionalized version of the Florida Keys. Oddly, it’s a slow-paced, slice-of-life section of the game that some players haven’t left yet, preferring to take it easy diving for treasure, fishing with Cal, and soaking up the environment. b396533c7816.title: Yes, There Was One Thing Cut from GTA 6 for Australia, NZ
b396533c7816.summary: Rockstar chopped out a temporary stat buff from GTA 6, although players down under may not ever really notice it.
b396533c7816.content: The Australian version of Grand Theft Auto 6 does differ from the international version in one small way; players down under are not able to use cocaine from their personal inventory to briefly overpower their stamina bar. NZ reportedly has the same version. In GTA 6, baggies of cocaine can be collected (or skimmed from full bricks) and show up as a consumable on the item wheel in the same section as cigarettes, cigars, and joints. Using one triggers a buff that puts stamina in an overpowered state, albeit only for about 30 seconds. This function was never included in the Australian-specific version of the game, as it would have prevented GTA 6 from being classified in the country until it was removed. Australia’s classification laws allow illicit drug use in games, but using them can’t provide the player with gameplay benefits. Overpowering your stamina (and everything else) is still possible via the use of adrenaline in the Australian version of GTA 6, and it’s also still possible to drink and smoke whenever you want. The general use of cocaine in story moments also still remains in the Australian version of GTA 6, because these instances aren’t associated with any in-game buffs. While the caveat that forbids rewards for illicit drug use is bespoke to Australia – and doesn’t apply to NZ – NZ’s rating system (which does piggyback on some Australian and UK classification decisions for unrestricted content ) has its own idiosyncrasies. These recently caught out IllFonic’s recent Halloween multiplayer game , which was refused classification in Australia for illicit drug use linked to an incentive or reward (that is, that use of the drug provides a gameplay advantage to the player). Halloween since made its way to NZ, but not Australia. Since this is not Rockstar’s first rodeo, it knew exactly the tweak GTA 6 would require to skirt this continuing quirk in Australian video game ratings and avoid multiple submissions.
